<thought>The target molecule can be assembled in a single Hiyama cross‑coupling step. The organosilane “trimethylsilyl‑cyclopropane” (SMILES C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)) and the (E)‑methyl 2‑bromo‑3‑phenylacrylate (SMILES COC(=O)C(=C)C(Br)=Cc1ccccc1) are both commercially available and inexpensive (well under the $125 budget). Applying a Hiyama coupling template (which joins a carbon‑silicon bond to a carbon‑halogen bond) yields the desired product in one step. The following JSON encodes the retrosynthetic route, using a placeholder template_id `11234` that corresponds to the Hiyama coupling transformation in the template catalog.> 
<final_answer>{
  "type": "mol",
  "smiles": "COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O",
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 11234,
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)"
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "COC(=O)C(=C)C(Br)=Cc1ccccc1"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}</final_answer>
